Not a bare identifier table on either side.
Every task cites at least one REQ-NNN: T-001 REQ-002/003/006 (tasks.md:158-159), T-002 REQ-002/003/006 (233-234), T-003 REQ-001 (290), T-004 REQ-004 (341), T-005 REQ-005 (395). No orphan task.

No task title contains test/spec/verify and no task's scope is exclusively test-file changes -- T-001/T-002 each edit runner scripts plus their suite (tasks.md:165-166, 240-241), T-003 edits the policy doc, T-004/T-005 edit docs/THREAT-MODEL.md. The check has no scoped surface to apply to; vacuously satisfied.

This is attempt 1 round 1, not a declared post-implementation provenance re-review (tasks.md:3 reads Task-Review-Status: Pending). All five tasks show Approval: Draft / Status: Planned (tasks.md:120-122, 210-212, 266-268, 319-321, 374-376), matching the pre-implementation rule exactly.

T-004 (tasks.md:323,332) and T-005 (tasks.md:378,386) each declare Risk: medium paired with Required Workflow: test-after. The risk-gate-matrix pairing this check enforces is low->test-after, medium->acceptance-first, high/critical->tdd, so both are mismatches (medium requires acceptance-first, not test-after). T-001/T-002 (high->tdd, tasks.md:124/143, 214/224) and T-003 (low->test-after, tasks.md:270/279) pair correctly. precheck-result.json's workflow_match_precheck is recorded PASS, but that field does not match a direct reading of these two tasks' own Risk/Required Workflow lines against the stated matrix, so this is not a duplicate of an already-caught precheck failure -- it is a distinct finding this check exists to catch. Both T-004 and T-005 carry security-sensitive judgement content (Risk Rationale at tasks.md:325-330 and 380-384 explicitly argue for medium over low because of anti-padding/omission risk), which is exactly the class of task the stricter acceptance-first workflow is meant to cover before implementation starts.

AC-003/AC-004/AC-011/AC-012 are claimed by both T-001 and T-002, and AC-005 by both T-001 and T-002, but each occurrence is explicitly runtime-scoped in the Requirements field text ('POSIX legs' tasks.md:158-159 vs 'PowerShell legs' tasks.md:233-234, 'PowerShell leg' tasks.md:233) and the task titles make the POSIX/PowerShell distinction explicit (tasks.md:116, 206). This matches the allowed distinct-scope exception; no unlabeled duplicate primary test target exists.

Every Blockers reference (T-002->T-001, T-003->T-002, T-004->T-003, T-005->T-004) resolves to a task ID present in both tasks.md and dependency-graph.json's nodes array (T-001..T-005). No dangling reference.
Runs because BLOCKERS-FORMAT is PASS. dependency-graph.json edges form a single linear chain T-005->T-004->T-003->T-002->T-001 with no back-edge; no node is revisited. No cycle.

T-001's 'and complete the exit-code contract' (tasks.md:116) is the same code change as the timeout it bounds (the bounded-wait helper's 124 return maps directly to the runner's exit code, design.md:59-84), not a second concern. T-004's 'OWASP LLM Top 10 and MCP cross-references' (tasks.md:315) and T-005's '...and close the residual risk' (tasks.md:370) both name sub-deliverables of a single requirement each (REQ-004 requirements.md:95-97 explicitly bundles OWASP+MCP as one requirement; REQ-005's traceability.md:19 summary explicitly bundles the five surfaces with the hook-trust bypass and this release's residual-risk closure). No task fuses two independent REQ-level concerns under one 'and'.

Every task's Done-When list contains at least one item naming a concrete verification command/evidence artifact: T-001 tasks.md:201-202 ('tests/cross-model.tests.sh passes, including every pre-existing case unmodified') and :203-204 ('verified by diff, not by assertion'); T-002 tasks.md:256-257; T-003 tasks.md:313 ('TEST-001 and TEST-002 pass in both suites', also names exact file/section at :296-298 since it is documentation-only); T-004 tasks.md:365-368; T-005 tasks.md:419 plus :420-421 ('verified by reading the file rather than assumed'). No item uses a forbidden bare verb (ensure/consider/verify is correct/works correctly/review without outcome/confirm without result), and no item asks to edit a review-frozen artifact (design.md, tasks.md body, or traceability.md) -- all target runner scripts, the policy doc, docs/THREAT-MODEL.md, or the two test suites.

traceability.md's Task Mapping table (56-62) lists T-001..T-005 matching tasks.md exactly; its Requirement Coverage table (13-20) lists REQ-001..REQ-006 matching requirements.md exactly. No dangling ID either direction. Full-profile layer-anchor check: every requirement row carries a canonical <layer>-spec.md#<section> anchor (none N/A).
